summary: `venture show` does not expose the venture version needed by `venture alias --input {expected_version}`
expected: A read command exposes the version an agent must echo back to a version-checked write.
actual: `venture show --id f0b5abfe…` returns {venture: {alias, created_at, id, name, objective, stage, workspace_id}} with no version; `venture alias` requires expected_version. I read ventures.version_id from the store read-only to set `v-crous-queue`.
reproduction: Run `venture show --id <venture>`; look for a version field; run `venture alias` with the expected_version it requires.
impact: An agent cannot set an alias through the public CLI without a read-only database query or trial and error.
suggestion: Include `version_id` in `venture show` (and in `agent resume` venture_state) and name it in the alias error message.
